A **Cayley graph** is a graph constructed from a group and a generating set; Cayley graphs are vertex-transitive.

**Strasser's conjecture.** Every connected Cayley graph is Hamiltonian.

$$
T^{(g)}(M_i)=T^{(g)}(N_i)

{"mathdb_id": 369042, "uuid": "efff0931-df05-44c5-91a6-2894fe2dfbc3", "canonical_url": "https://mathdb.com/p/369042/classification-conjecture-for-abelian-cayley-graphs-with-one", "title": "Classification conjecture for abelian Cayley graphs with one symmetry class of Hamiltonian cycles", "statement": "Let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group with generating set $S$, and let $G=\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$. Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the class of graphs having a unique Hamiltonian cycle up to symmetry. **Abelian Cayley-graph classification conjecture.** Then

$$
G\in\mathcal{H}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\in\{C_4\mathbin{\square}K_2,\ C_n,\ K_n,\ K_{n,n},\ C_k\mathbin{\square}K_2: n,k\in\mathbb{N},\ k\text{ odd}\}.

Write $R(N)$ for the set of rooted triples displayed by a network $N$, and write $N_1\cong N_2$ when the networks are isomorphic. **Rooted-triple reconstruction conjecture.** If $N_1$ and $N_2$ have no near-sibling reticulations, then

$$
R(N_1)=R(N_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_1\cong N_2.

Let $X$ be the leaf set, and let $N_1$ and $N_2$ be binary normal networks on $X$ with no near-sibling reticulations. Write $R(N)$ for the set of rooted triples displayed by a network $N$, and write $N_1\cong N_2$ when the networks are isomorphic. **Rooted-triple reconstruction conjecture.** If $N_1$ and $N_2$ have no near-sibling reticulations, then

$$
R(N_1)=R(N_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_1\cong N_2.
$$

The paper's main theorem proves this reconstruction statement under the stronger assumption that both networks have no near reticulations, while examples show that excluding near-sibling reticulations is necessary in general. Whether the weaker hypothesis also suffices when near-stack reticulations are allowed remains open.

$$
s_1\leqslant s_2\leqslant t_2\leqslant t_1,
$$

and with $R(a,b)$ denoting the two-colour Ramsey number, **the Ramsey diagonal conjecture.** If

$$
s_1+t_1\leqslant s_2+t_2,
$$

then

$$
R(s_1,t_1)\leqslant R(s_2,t_2).
